Thanks again for the SIG submission last week. Our audit team has a follow-up: they need more granular RTO/RPO evidence related to your multi-region failover and warm-cache behavior for sessioned inference workloads. Specifically they're asking for:

- a matrix of nominal RTO/RPO targets by service tier and model family (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- artifacts from a recent DR test that show measured failover times (start -> traffic cutover -> full KV cache warm)
- a short description of how prefix/KV cache warming is handled during regional failover and expected impact on tail latency
- any runbooks or playbooks used during the test and evidence that the runbook was followed (attestation, test owner, timestamps)

Can you provide these items, or point us to the specific files/drive folder in the next 48 hours? We're trying to close the SIG review by EOD next Tuesday.

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you requested; attaching an initial RTO/RPO matrix and the DR test summary from our March regional failover exercise. Quick notes up front:

- Our RTO/RPO targets are tiered: Hosted API (SLA customers) = RTO 5m / RPO 0s (KV persisted with geo-replication), Dedicated = RTO 10m / RPO 0-30s (config dependent), Private/VPC = customer-dependent but typical guidance is RTO 1h / RPO 0-30m documented in contracts.
- The attached DR test summary documents a simulated us-west failure at 2027-03-01T02:00Z with automated routing to us-east; measured traffic cutover (DNS + routing rules) took 3m40s; KV cache rebuild to 80% warm for hot prefixes observed at ~9m.
- We include screenshots of runbook checkpoints and an audit log excerpt (redacted for IPs) showing the playbook steps.

Attachments included: rto_rpo_matrix_v2.pdf, dr_test_summary_2027-03-01.xlsx, redwood_datacenter_zone_map.png

If the auditor needs raw logs (auditd/timestamps) we can provision a time-limited Drive link or a zipped bundle; let us know the minimum retention window you need.

I can also set up a 30-min technical walkthrough with Rishi and Priyom to go over cache behavior and metrics. Proposed times: Mon 10am PT or Tue 2pm PT.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman

Hi Mark/Jenna — adding technical context and contractual pointer. Short answers:

- Contractual remedies: For Dedicated we offer a tiered credit schedule tied to missed availability/RTO SLAs in the customer contract; for Private deployments we provide a remediation plan and can negotiate service credits on a case-by-case basis governed by the SLA addendum. Naomi can share the standard SLA language excerpt under a CDA if needed.

- On cache warming: our runtime uses a two-stage warming approach during failover: (1) traffic steering + prefix-preserving routing ensures requests hit warm nodes where possible, (2) background KV prefetch prioritizes top-k prefixes by recent access; full parity (all prefixes) depends on traffic patterns and typically hits 80-95% warm within 8-12 minutes in our measured tests.

- The attached DR test workbook includes timeline slices and per-service latency distributions during failover. Notes on measurement methodology are in the workbook appendix.

If you want the raw timestamps for the audit binder we can generate a signed CSV export. We prefer to redact internal IPs but can provide traceroute / BGP event IDs on request.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
